title: Channel File 291
oneLine: A routine content update for CrowdStrike's Windows sensor blue-screened the Windows hosts that loaded it.

sources.title: Falcon Content Update Preliminary Post Incident Report | CrowdStrike

facts.label: Exposure window
facts.quote: online between Friday, July 19, 2024 04:09 UTC and Friday, July 19, 2024 05:27 UTC

facts.label: Crash
facts.quote: resulting in a Windows operating system crash (BSOD)

facts.label: Sensors hit
facts.quote: Windows hosts running sensor version 7.11 and above

facts.label: Mac and Linux
facts.quote: Mac and Linux hosts were not impacted.

events.label: Content update released
events.quote: CrowdStrike released a content configuration update for the Windows sensor

events.label: Update reverted
events.quote: The defect in the content update was reverted on Friday, July 19, 2024 at 05:27 UTC.

levers.label: Rollout
levers.why: The update reached every online Windows sensor in the window
levers.quote: Implement a staggered deployment strategy for Rapid Response Content in which updates are gradually deployed to larger portions of the sensor base, starting with a canary deployment.

levers.label: Content Validator
levers.why: A validator bug let the bad template instance through
levers.quote: Add additional validation checks to the Content Validator for Rapid Response Content.

levers.label: Error handling
levers.why: The out-of-bounds read could not be handled gracefully
levers.quote: Enhance existing error handling in the Content Interpreter.

levers.label: Release to revert
levers.why: The report gives no time for the first alert, so this counts from the release
levers.quote: Improve monitoring for both sensor and system performance, collecting feedback during Rapid Response Content deployment to guide a phased rollout.

afterwards.quote: Implement a staggered deployment strategy for Rapid Response Content in which updates are gradually deployed to larger portions of the sensor base, starting with a canary deployment.
Provide customers with greater control over the delivery of Rapid Response Content updates by allowing granular selection of when and where these updates are deployed.
Add additional validation checks to the Content Validator for Rapid Response Content.
Enhance existing error handling in the Content Interpreter.

assumptions.what: Every host that loads the update crashes and serves nothing
assumptions.why: The report says loading the file crashed Windows. It gives no count of hosts.

assumptions.what: Crashed hosts stay down after the revert
assumptions.why: The report says hosts online in the window were affected and later ones were not. It does not describe crashed hosts recovering on their own.

assumptions.what: Detection is counted from the moment the change landed
assumptions.why: The postmortem gives no time for the first alert.

assumptions.what: The change reaches every server within a few seconds
assumptions.why: The postmortem does not say how fast it spread.

assumptions.what: Each staged rollout step waits 10 minutes, and early stages carry 1 to 2% of traffic each
assumptions.why: Used only when you switch the rollout to staged. The postmortem does not describe a staged path.
